ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a transition-state structure, with R¹ and R² on the left connected to the central carbon; the central carbon is also connected to the N above and the carbon below. The N above has H, but the N-H bond is not counted according to the problem statement. On the right, a carbonyl carbon can be seen connected to O by a double bond and connected to another O by a single bond; this O is also connected to the carbon below. The carbon below is also connected to a nitrogen labeled HN, and bonds involving H are not counted. The curved arrows in the figure only indicate electron movement and are ignored according to the problem statement. Reasoning: Count one by one the bonds that do not involve hydrogen and are not arrows: R¹-central C, R²-central C, central C-N above, central C-carbon below, N above-carbonyl C, carbonyl C=O, carbonyl C-O, O-carbon below, carbon below-NH, for a total of 9 bonds.

method.method_draft: Scan the image bond by bond, excluding all arrows and any bond involving H. Count the visible non-hydrogen connections: R1-central C, R2-central C, central C-upper N, central C-lower carbon, upper N-carbonyl C, carbonyl C=O, carbonyl C-O, O-lower carbon, and lower carbon-NH. This gives 9 bonds.
